implementation_notes: doobie models the store as a pure program: the record is a case class with Read/Write instances, the append is sql"INSERT INTO msg_store ...".update.run (a ConnectionIO, a description rather than an effect), and execution happens through a Transactor[IO] built over a connection pool, so the classic Store object becomes a few small composable actions with resource management and retry supplied by cats-effect. The tap is a bounded cats-effect Queue: the delivery code only offers the record (tryOffer) and a single background fiber drains it through the transactor, which is what serialises writers and keeps store failures off the request fiber. Retention is another action - a DELETE by timestamp run on a schedule - and reporting is a query action executed in parallel by readers.
pitfalls: Running the store action on the request fiber couples business latency to the database; the delivery path should only offer to a bounded Queue (tryOffer) and count the drops.
A Transactor pool with more than one writer breaks SQLite with SQLITE_BUSY: size the pool to a single connection for the writer and give readers their own.
Implicit Read/Write derivation follows the case class, so adding or renaming a field silently breaks de-serialisation of old rows unless the payload is stored as an explicit JSON string.
Fiber failures in the draining fiber are invisible unless surfaced: the queue's failure and drop signals are the store's health metric.

variants.name: Slick lifted table mapping (DBIO actions)
variants.implementation_notes: Slick's lifted embedding makes the store one more mapped table: a TableQuery[MStored] with typed columns, the append a DBIO action (messages += record), and execution a db.run(append.transactionally) against a Database backed by a JDBC driver, so the classic Store interface is replaced by a table object plus actions that compose into transactions. Choose this variant when the application already speaks Slick and the audit table should share its session and transaction style; choose the doobie variant when the codebase is tagless-final and the store should stay a plain SQL action. Retention is a delete query action run on a schedule, and reporting is any Slick query over the same table.
pitfalls: DBIO actions are values: an append that is built but never run records nothing, and running it outside the intended transaction loses atomicity.
Slick's AsyncExecutor thread pool is shared; an audit load that saturates it starves business queries, so give the store its own executor or bound the tap.
SQLite plus connection pooling multiplies writers again (SQLITE_BUSY); one writer connection and WAL remain the configuration.
Nested transactions without savepoints flatten into the outer transaction, so an audit rollback can undo business work - keep the store's transaction separate.
